科研.title: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets
科研.summary: arXiv:2611.14544v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets has been studied as a handwriting-recognition problem: read the move in each box and check that it is legal. This framing misses the errors that matter most. A misread that yields an illegal move is loud. One that yields a legal-but-wrong move is silent, because a legality-only pipeline accepts it and reads every later move against a wrong position. We therefore treat the task as game reconstruction and present Zugwise, which repurposes computer-chess machinery (quiescence search, static exchange evaluation, pin detection) to ask not "what should be played?" but "could a human plausibly have written this?" An absurdity detector makes silent errors loud at or near where they occur, and a backward search traces late symptoms to their cause. Candidate ranking excludes chess-quality signals. A Needleman-Wunsch merge adds the second player's sheet as evidence, and review stops send every disagreement between the sheets' legal readings to a human. In oracle replay of two tournament sections, a release adding them cuts silent errors from 16 to 1 and from 50 to 13. Two learned signals, CTC re-scoring against the recognizer's raw output and a Maia-style human-move prior, raise the correct fix's top-rank rate from 58.8% to 78.0% of the replacement decisions where it is a candidate, and hold without refitting on a later section. On the first section, the human-verified output matches an independent expert transcription move for move on 34 of 45 games, and adjudication against the sheets found errors in both records, on different plies. We do not establish that either workflow is faster or more accurate. The system runs entirely in the browser and is free, private, and offline-capable; alongside it we offer a three-way adjudication protocol for a domain where no single record is ground truth.

科研.title: Cleaning an Agent's History Hurts When the World Still Holds the Error
科研.summary: arXiv:2611.14654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents accumulate histories of their own mistakes, and a system that compacts, repairs or hands off such a history decides what it says about those mistakes while their effects stay in the world. Prior work cleans the history at a fixed world, where showing a corrected step and saying it is done move together. We ask whether the same correct content helps or hurts depending on how the history states it and what the world holds. We freeze an agent mid-task with its exact world state, edit the history or the world, and let a receiver model continue. On AgentCE-Bench, after the agent commits a wrong value, we hold the world fixed and add the correct value by two natural edits: a truthful note beside the preserved error or the agent's own completed action. The note raises recovery, the share of remaining targets the receiver gets right, from 51% under a matched neutral note to 66%. The completed action lowers it below the unedited history, from 50% to 44%, so the value's presence alone does not predict the effect. On AppWorld, after a database write, we vary whether its receipt reports success or failure and whether its effect is present. A success receipt lowers whole-task success from 45% to 28% while the effect is absent and raises it from 38% to 49% once present. The two effects differ by 27 points pooled over two receivers, a difference positive in six of eight receivers at 97.5% and seven at 95%. A history edit's effect thus depends on the world it describes, and a history made to look clean while the world still holds the error can leave an agent worse off than no edit at all.

科研.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
科研.summary: arXiv:2611.14681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Today's AI workloads are rapidly changing: new models are released more often, model architectures are increasingly diverse, and traffic distributions change frequently. The challenge we face at Together AI is continual optimization for these changing workloads. Compiling a deployment into an optimized forward pass is a challenge that is well-suited for agent hill-climbing. Existing systems struggle with continual compilation due to a tradeoff between measurement throughput and fidelity. Many systems use agents to optimize individual kernels from the inference forward pass using offline benchmarks, but timings are low-fidelity because of data-dependent behavior in primitives like mixture-of-experts (MoE). On the other hand, systems use agents to directly optimize end-to-end engines but suffer from slow engine launch times. To address these challenges, we build Together Compiler (TKCC), the first truly continual agent loop designed for AI inference optimization. To address the throughput-fidelity tradeoff, we propose: (1) a Tiered Persistent Engine that decouples engine launch overheads from forward pass computation; (2) a cost model to select the parallelism configurations that seed the optimization process. We also conduct extensive ablations on agent context management and present our insights on deploying TKCC in production. TKCC outperforms highly-optimized hand-written Megakernels on the Llama 1B workhorse workload by up to 1.7x and the best open source engines on the latest frontier models (Kimi K3, GLM 5.3, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, DeepSeek v4.1 Flash) across hardware platforms by up to 2.6x higher TPS on the InferenceX benchmark. TKCC also sets the state-of-the-art performance at batch size 1, with 1111 TPS on M3.1 Flash and 1205 TPS on DeepSeek v4.1 Flash. Finally, TKCC generalizes beyond frontier language model inference. TKCC serves trillions of tokens across our production fleet.

科研.title: When Should Semantic Priors Enter Partially-Identified Causal Discovery?
科研.summary: arXiv:2611.14736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Observational causal discovery often leaves causal di- rections unresolved or unstable. Large language mod- els (LLMs) can provide semantic information to resolve these directions, but incorrect proposals can exclude the true causal graph and invalidate downstream inference. We study three separate decisions: where to allocate semantic queries, which proposals to admit, and which causal graphs to retain. Our framework distinguishes population non-identifiability from finite-sample insta- bility, evaluates semantic orientation against statistical and random controls, and examines calibrated admis- sion and error-tolerant DAG retention. Experiments across benchmark networks show that semantic infor- mation improves recovery over coin-flip orientations, but targeting unstable edges has no established ad- vantage over matched-random allocation. The tested admission certificate cannot support nontrivial admis- sion with the available calibration tasks. Moreover, downstream retention depends on reference adequacy: learned references contain the true DAG in only three of 80 planned tasks. These findings separate the value of semantic information from the reliability of its alloca- tion, admission, and retention, and identify calibration size and reference adequacy as key limitations.

科研.title: SynthCorp: A Platform for Creating Benchmarks for Data Agents
科研.summary: arXiv:2611.14765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current benchmarks for LLM-driven data agents saturate quickly and cannot target specific capabilities. We present SynthCorp, a platform that creates customizable data estates and benchmarks by simulating how business events produce and modify corporate data over time. Each data estate combines relational databases, a document store, and a data catalog, paired with evaluation tasks and executable gold programs. First, given a scenario and target complexity dimensions, SynthCorp synthesizes reusable event types and compiles each into a program over predefined simulation primitives. Second, SynthCorp schedules event instances on a virtual calendar, interleaving routine and disruption events so that tables, documents, and catalog entries remain consistent. Third, SynthCorp executes the calendar to materialize the data estate and records every operation in a simulation log. Fourth, SynthCorp generates analytical tasks and derives verified gold programs from the log. We use SynthCorp to generate initial evaluation benchmarks comprising seven data estates (up to 1K operational tables) and 256 tasks across five domains. The data estates pass deterministic pipeline checks (such as foreign-key violations, undeclared writes, recurrence violations, and database execution failures) with a near-zero error rate, introduce cross-asset complexities, and cover all requested dimensions. Evaluating three models across four data-context settings shows that the benchmarks separate data contexts and model tiers. Auditing candidate queries against causal provenance in the simulation log verifies gold programs without manual annotation, including on multi-event composite tasks that expose reasoning failures in state-of-the-art agents. We hope the community uses SynthCorp to generate more challenging and useful data estates and benchmarks that foster the development of enterprise data agents.

科研.title: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI
科研.summary: arXiv:2611.14766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: All social interactions are situated in time. Previous studies have shown that humans are able to use implicit temporal cues, such as the duration of a pause, to infer others' mental states. But how do humans use temporal cues for dynamic, fine-grained social coordination? And can AI systems do the same, without ``experiencing'' continuous real-time as humans do? We study these questions using a cooperative card game task called The Mind, which requires players to achieve a shared goal across repeated interactions but forbids explicit communication: the only available signal is the passage of time. We evaluate 150 humans, and two classes of AI models which reflect different ways of operationalizing time in artificial systems: computer-use agents (CUAs), and standard text-prompted LLMs. We find that human behavior is best captured by a Bayesian strategy that infers a partner's belief from their timing---and similarly for frontier models. However, unlike humans, none of the tested models seem to efficiently adapt their behaviors to their partners' over the course of the game. From a cognitive perspective, our findings suggest that humans perform implicit probabilistic reasoning about continuous-time signals in dynamic social settings, and that such reasoning mechanisms may emerge without real-time experience. Practically, our study highlights new challenges for AI systems to coordinate efficiently with other agents by learning to interpret and adapt to their implicit signals in dynamic settings.

科研.title: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
科研.summary: arXiv:2611.14769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Arena-style rankings of language models are a widely used evaluation framework in online leaderboards, research papers, and model evaluation in production. These rankings aim to realistically assess model performance using pairwise comparisons of anonymous models on user prompts, aggregating votes via the Bradley-Terry model to produce the final ranking. However, we find that these leaderboards are highly vulnerable to several manipulation strategies that unscrupulous providers could use to boost a model's rank: strategic voting (individual votes that boost a model's rank, including votes on irrelevant models), strategic prompting (choosing prompts that favor a model), and strategic nomination (boosting the rank of a model by inserting irrelevant models). We demonstrate these effects on public leaderboard data, analyze the circumstances that cause these vulnerabilities, and describe approaches to safeguard against each attack. Notably, these issues hold for any preference-based evaluation using the Bradley-Terry model that allows open prompting, voting, or model submission. These manipulations boost the rank of nearly every tested model; each attack can boost a model by up to 15-20 places in a ranking and, combined, they can boost a model by up to 45 places.

科研.title: Robust Task-Aware State Estimation from Pre-trained Perception
科研.summary: arXiv:2611.14781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents that perform state estimation using pretrained perception models, e.g., Vision-Language Models (VLMs), face the fundamental challenge that predictions are uncertain. Still, most approaches determinize these predictions into a single best-guess state and make decisions as if it were ground truth. This is brittle because when the guess is wrong, the agent's decisions may be unsafe or infeasible. At the other extreme, maintaining a full probability distribution over symbolic states is often intractable. We propose a middle path, drawing on the underlying probabilities the perception model already produces (e.g., a VLM's output-layer token distributions) to construct a $\theta$-confidence Minimal Belief Set (MBS$_\theta$), a minimal subset of states whose cumulative probability meets a user-specified belief-mass threshold. The minimality of an MBS$_\theta$ ensures that the agent considers only the most likely states, enhancing robustness in downstream decision-making while maintaining computational tractability. Using a novel three-layered belief system, we efficiently approximate individual state probabilities from per-feature predictions and task-level constraints. On this belief construction, we base our MBS$_\theta$ construction, while maintaining only a lean factored representation of the belief. Our algorithm, Probability-Ranked Valid State Search (PRaVaSS), takes advantage of the unique structure of this belief system to construct an MBS$_\theta$ with correctness guarantees and polynomial complexity in the unconstrained case. Using a VLM as the backbone of our state estimator, we validate our method's theoretical properties, scalability with problem size, and improvement of downstream decision-making when used in a task-planning pipeline.

科技.summary: IT之家 11 月 14 日消息，2026 年 TCL 华星全球显示生态大会（DTC2026）昨日（13 日）举行，推出印刷 OLED 氧化物内补 QHD 500Hz 电竞显示 (27")。 据财联社报道，TCL 科技集团高级副总裁、TCL 华星首席执行官赵军接受采访时表示， 该产品正在进行相应的开发和进一步完善 ，具体上市时间需根据品牌客户的产品规划节奏确定。 对于市场关注的印刷 OLED 产线爬坡情况，赵军表示，目前武汉的 t12 产线生产情况良好，产能已从过去的每月 3K 大板提升至 9K 大板，且产线良率提升迅速， 首款产品 4 月投入量产后，良率已从刚投产时的个位数提升至目前的约 70% 。目前，有 多款印刷 OLED 产品正同时处于量产状态 。 据IT之家了解， 印刷 OLED 采用喷墨打印工艺 ，将有机发光材料以“按需沉积”方式精准印刷到玻璃基板上，相比传统真空蒸镀，具备材料利用率更高、生产更绿色高效等显著优势。 相关阅读： 《 TCL 华星 CEO 赵军：印刷 OLED 已实现量产出货，广州 t8 项目计划明年 5 月产品点亮 》

科技.title: 谷歌利用多个专业 AI 智能体打造 Teamwork 系统，成功验证多项复杂数学证明
科技.summary: IT之家 11 月 14 日消息，谷歌宣布进一步扩展旗下 Antigravity 多智能体系统，利用多个由 Gemini 模型驱动的专业智能体组成 Teamwork 系统，号称可解决“长期悬而未决的数学难题”、“验证复杂数学证明”，并优化各种软件系统性能。 例如，谷歌已成功对韦伊猜想（Weil conjectures）进行形式化证明。这是一组关于有限域上多项式方程解的数量的重要数学结论，最初由数学家皮埃尔 · 德利涅（Pierre Deligne）于 1974 年证明。谷歌 Teamwork-LEAP 系统通过约 2.88 万次子智能体调用，累计生成约 180 万行 Lean 代码，完成了相关数学成果的形式化工作。 谷歌还表示，相应系统近期还成功复现了一项关于三维纳维-斯托克斯方程（Navier–Stokes equations）有限时间爆破问题的形式化证明。并帮助研究人员解决了库尔塔德-库马尔猜想（Courtade–Kumar conjecture）。 从技术层面，谷歌 Teamwork 系统主要依靠多个智能体并行工作，并安排独立系统对提出的解答进行质疑和验证，以减少单个 AI 模型在生成长篇推理过程中可能出现的错误。每个专业智能体只能访问完成任务所需的文件和工具，随后由独立的质疑者和审查者检查结果，而不依赖原始智能体的推理过程。 除了数学研究，谷歌还将这套技术应用于分子化学领域。一支由 30 个专业智能体组成的团队，配合融入物理知识的模拟器，利用核磁共振（NMR）数据识别分子结构。在复杂分子基准测试中，该系统的 Top-1 准确率达到 95%，Top-3 准确率达到 100%。 在系统工程领域，谷歌也展示了多智能体协作的应用成果。该公司表示，其智能体团队将自家的 libgav1 AV1 视频解码器从 C++ 重写为 Rust，最终生成约 17 万行代码，并在一套覆盖范围广泛的测试中实现了与原始版本完全一致的输出结果。 目前，谷歌正通过 Antigravity 向用户开放 Teamwork 系统，以及名为 /boost 的迭代式编程工作流，计划向 1 万名学术研究人员提供为期 6 个月的最高使用额度免费访问权限。

科技.title: 堪比蓝屏“灭霸”事件：微软 2026 最严重宕机重创全球金融业，交易员被迫改用传真
科技.summary: IT之家 11 月 14 日消息，据新加坡《商业时报》昨日（11 月 13 日）报道，受微软多项软件服务全球性故障影响， 全球金融业务遭受重创，部分交易员被迫改用电话、WhatsApp，甚至重新启用传真机维持业务运转。 从东京到休斯敦，各交易台都用不了邮件系统，而交易确认、价格报告和客户联络都要靠它。新加坡交易员反映，一些银行无法完成融资交易；泛欧交易所、纳斯达克和德意志交易所均报告电子邮件问题。印度券商则提醒客户，邮件咨询回复可能延迟；而日本部分公司通过传真处理交易。 CMC Markets 新加坡的销售交易员 Eugene Koh 表示平时一封邮件、一秒钟能完成的事情，如今可能需要打电话、花上几分钟，而且“大家又都拿起了电话, 我们的 WhatsApp 聊天群也比平时更忙了。” 法国巴黎资产管理的高级债券策略师 Ryutaro Kimura 表示虽然他所在的机构受到的影响较小，交易本身大体未受影响，但交易确认信息积压，给后台结算带来压力。 这次故障发生时, 石油交易员正面对美伊和谈消息引发的油价剧烈波动。BOK Financial Securities 交易部高级副总裁丹尼斯 · 基斯勒 (Dennis Kissler) 说, 他的团队过了一个小时才发现邮件发不出去, 随后才开始逐一给客户打电话。他对彭博社表示:“我们当时陷入了一个小时的黑洞。” 标普全球旗下的普氏 (Platts) 警告称, 价格更新可能会延迟, 并请市场参与者通过电话或即时通讯工具提供信息。普氏还表示，在问题修复之前，22 项生物燃料价格将暂停发布。 问题始于美国东部时间 11 月 12 日 (周四) 中午之后。大约一小时内, 故障监测网站 Downdetector 就收到了来自 74 个国家和地区的故障报告。报告量峰值达到每分钟 19,650 条, 而平常的周四每分钟不到 15 条。 微软起初将原因归结为其多个地区基础设施上的 " 负载升高 ", 随后暂停了部署并重启服务器。后来微软表示, 负责建立安全连接的一个进程不堪重负, 导致服务器停止处理请求。 此次宕机让世界各地的政府机构、交易员和企业陷入停摆。英国多地警方无法接收网上报案，药剂师警告称处方配药可能延误。日本的政府共用 IT 平台、从洛杉矶到新加坡的多地法院，以及澳大利亚的情报机构和联邦警察机构也受到影响。 微软周五（11 月 13 日）表示，已修复 Microsoft 365 故障的根本原因。这次故障持续近 24 小时，导致 Outlook 瘫痪，数十个国家的用户在使用 Teams 和 Copilot 时也受到影响。 CNBC 等多家媒体称这是“微软 2026 最大宕机事件”， 澳大利亚内政部长托尼 · 伯克（Tony Burke）认为本次宕机事件造成的破坏和影响力，堪比 2024 年的 CrowdStrike 全球蓝屏“灭霸”宕机事故。 IT之家注：蓝屏“灭霸”事件发生于 2024 年 7 月 19 日，本来负责保护电脑的网络安全公司，因为一次错误更新，让全球大量 Windows 设备集体蓝屏、反复重启，进而扰乱航空、银行、医疗和广播等服务。微软初步估计，约 850 万台 Windows 设备受到影响。 微软表示：“对于此次事件给客户和合作伙伴造成的干扰，我们深表歉意”，并称“各项服务正在大范围恢复，运行趋于稳定”。微软在 X 平台上发帖称，“这是一个与网络攻击或 AI / 智能体无关的技术问题”。
